summary: Replaces the vulnerable archive reader with bounded in-memory ZIP processing and upgrades request logging to the patched Morgan release.
userImpact: Configuration bundle and project archive imports retain their existing interfaces and never extract files onto the server filesystem.

instructions: Upgrade the backend and matching shared and host packages to consume the patched dependencies.

configuration: No environment variable changes. Configuration ZIPs retain their existing JSON envelope and byte/file limits and now reject unsupported ZIP metadata before processing.
security: Removes adm-zip, affected by CVE-2026-76845, without downgrading to versions affected by earlier archive vulnerabilities.
Candidate image acceptance continues to reject all vulnerability severities; no advisory exceptions are added.
documentation: Dependency notices identify the patched request logger; docs/development/archive-imports.md describes the bounded reader, supported ZIP subset and import limits.
knownLimitations: ZIP imports accept stored/deflated single-disk UTF-8 archives; ZIP64, multipart, encrypted and special-file archives must be re-exported as ordinary ZIPs. Project imports are limited to 25 MiB compressed, 100 MiB uncompressed and 10,000 entries; configuration archives retain 1 MiB and 64-file limits with a 128-record metadata ceiling.
rollback: Restoring the earlier image reintroduces vulnerable dependencies; prefer a forward fix. No database rollback is required.
validation: Archive/logging regressions, including real streaming exports, dishonest sizes, CRC, overlap and descriptor rejection; PostgreSQL route export/import round trip.
Backend and host package builds/type checks; eight packed package contracts; dependency/readiness/classifier contracts; notices and documentation boundary checks.

Pinned candidate Trivy scanner rejects all severities; the rebuilt local backend and unchanged exact candidate frontend digest both passed without new ignore entries. Protected CI still qualifies the proposed revision and candidate images.
